current_leader.name: Cloud support-plan right-sizing engine
current_leader.state_transition: monthly cloud spend and support-case/incident telemetry update -> current paid support tier cost recomputed -> compare observed support need/risk with cheaper eligible tier -> recommend KEEP/DOWNGRADE/UPGRADE at next permissible boundary -> verify support-fee delta
current_leader.why_survived: AWS support pricing is recurring, percentage/minimum-based and can produce large deterministic fee deltas. Billing and support telemetry are independent machine-readable triggers. Current searches found first-party price calculators and plan-change workflows but not a continuous support-utilization-aware right-sizing engine.
current_leader.strongest_evidence: AWS Business Support+ is priced at the greater of $29/account or 9%/7%/5%/3% of monthly charges; Enterprise Support is the greater of $5,000/month or 10%/7%/5%/3%; Unified Operations has a $50,000 monthly minimum. Paid plans are monthly and AWS documents Support/Trusted Advisor APIs and plan-change workflows.
current_leader.closest_threat: AWS exposes plan comparison, pricing calculation and downgrade workflows; broad FinOps/MSP providers can absorb the advice. Enterprise downgrades require TAM contact. No exact continuous optimizer was found in this run.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read billing forecast, support tier, support-case/incident history and required support features; output KEEP/DOWNGRADE/UPGRADE plus next-month fee delta and feature/risk tradeoff; no automatic plan change.
current_leader.monetization: Per verified plan-change event, low fixed monthly fee, or capped share of verified support-fee savings for a defined measurement window.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Actual support-tier overprovisioning is unquantified and support is partly tail-risk insurance; a static annual review may capture most value.
current_leader.next_research_test: Find evidence of material support-tier overpayment, measure how often the optimal tier changes, and search FinOps/MSP products specifically for continuous support-plan right-sizing. Demote/reject if mostly static or already productized.

recent_cross_family_findings: Cloud support-plan right-sizing promoted: recurring percentage/minimum fee, independent billing/support telemetry and deterministic delta; exact continuous optimizer not found.
Merchant settlement acceleration demoted to runner-up because avoidable acceleration remains unproven and willingness-to-pay suggests rational liquidity demand.
Vacant-unit utility recovery rejected: exact products already automate vacancy detection, chargebacks, deposit recovery and cost allocation.
Generic SaaS license reclamation rejected: exact tools already map activity to entitlements and reclaim idle seats.
Freight accessorial/rate audit remains rejected; fresh exact tools continue to cover the micro-events.

New rule: support/service tiers qualify as programmable money flows only when tier sufficiency can be inferred from independent telemetry, but tail-risk value must be modeled rather than treating low usage as waste.
known_rejected_or_demoted_summary: Full historical rejection list is preserved in prior anchor blobs and immutable run files. Do not revive prior rejected families without materially new mechanism/evidence.
